candidate_relations.reason: Thyrotoxicosis names the hormone state but omits Graves disease as the required etiology.
Psychosis due to thyrotoxicosis is a neuropsychiatric manifestation, not the requested Graves diagnosis.
Mood disorder describes the behavioral presentation rather than the thyroid etiology.
A manic episode due to thyrotoxicosis is a psychiatric manifestation of Graves thyrotoxicosis.
Anxiety disorder captures a symptom cluster but not the underlying Graves disease.
A TSH-secreting pituitary tumor would elevate TSH, whereas TSH was suppressed below 0.01 mU/L.
Hyperthyroidism is the parent hormone state but lacks Graves-specific etiology.
Thyroid storm is a more severe decompensated state; temperature was 36.7°C without storm criteria.
A psychotic disorder labels the mental-status change rather than Graves disease.
Anxiety disorder due to thyrotoxicosis is a psychiatric manifestation of the thyroid disease.
Pheochromocytoma does not suppress TSH or produce a diffuse goitre and lid lag.
A manic episode is the behavioral state, not the Graves diagnosis.
Hyperthyroidism due to thyroiditis asserts a destructive etiology incompatible with Graves.
Thyrotoxic crisis is an alias of thyroid storm and overstates severity relative to this presentation.
Graves' disease is a harmless alias of the reference diagnosis, supported by thyrotoxicosis, smooth goitre, and lid lag.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Graves' disease alias of Graves disease
